methods.label: Split along the horizontal diagonal
methods.explanation:
Join the leftmost and rightmost vertices of the quadrilateral. They lie in the same horizontal row, so this diagonal gives a convenient base for two triangles.

Count the gaps between pegs: the diagonal has length \(4\) units. The upper vertex is \(2\) rows above it, and the lower vertex is \(1\) row below it. Since adjacent rows are one unit apart, the corresponding perpendicular heights are \(2\) and \(1\) units.

The two triangles fill the quadrilateral and share only their base, so their areas add:
\[
\frac12\cdot4\cdot2+\frac12\cdot4\cdot1
=4+2=\boxed{6}\text{ square units}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Splitting the quadrilateral into two triangles requires only unit-gap counting and the elementary base-height area formula.
